newsitem.title: USA: Madsen Gold ceo says to start production in May.
newsitem.headline: Madsen Gold ceo says to start production in May.

text.p: Madsen Gold Corp, a Toronto-listed Canadian gold explorer, will start production from its mine at Red Lake, Ontario, in May, company president James Morlock said in an interview with Reuters.
The company has already hedged most of the first years output at prices around $360-380 an ounce, he added.

"We've made great strides in the past year, we bought a mill very cheaply from Placer Dome, we've got a stockpile of ore ready to go through the system, we've got pretty much a full complement of staff, we've raised the production finance we need, and it's all falling into shape," Morlock said.
"We anticipate starting production in May," he said.
Madsen expects production of 40,000 ounces of gold from Red Lake in the first year and 50,000 ounces in the second year.
"We've sold forward 2,000 ounces a month commencing in June and July this year, and we did that on the spike in the gold price a couple of months back at $365 an ounce or C$510," Morlock said.
After seeing a four year low around $336.00 an ounce in January this year, spot gold prices recovered to a $363 in early March, before sliding back to $339.50 Tuesday morning.

"Under our borrowing provisions we've taken only gold loans and hedged those selling forward another 12,000 oz in the C$480-500 range, so in fact we've sold forward 38,000 oz of the projected 40,000 oz in the first year and are very well hedged," he said.
"And in years two and three we are hedged at even better prices," he said.
"We are also active on the Canadian/U.S. dollar as we feel the Canadian is oversold."
Before shutting down in 1976, the old Madsen gold mine in the Red Lake camp in northwestern Ontario produced over 2.4 million ounces of gold from 1938 onwards.
But new technology has allowed the former producer, now wholly owned by Madsen Gold, to rehabilitate the old workings and define new levels of reserves.
Total proven and probable reserves now total about 1.1 million tonnes, grading at 0.28 ounces of gold per tonne.
"The Red Lake camp was one of the richest in North America, hosted by the Campbell mine and we've put together about 10,000 contiguous acres of claims there," Morlock said.

Unfortunateley stock prices of Canadian miners fell heavily in recent weeks in the wake of the problems surrounding Canadian miner, Bre-X Minerals Ltd, and Madsen's stock was no exception, but Madsen Gold already had its production finance in place, Morlock said.
"We raised about $10-12 million in the past year or two, and have production finance of $5 million from Standard Bank, plus a contingency standby of $1 million," he said.
Madsen arranged a project financing facility for $5 million, or the gold equivalent, in February this year, with Standard Bank London and Standard New York.
"There's probably also another $1 million to come from the exercise of warrants in the next 12 months."
The company expects total cash costs to be $250 an ounce in the first full year, but hopes to eventually lower these costs to around $240 an ounce.
"We won't be taxable for the first four years and we expect the company to show profits, not just cash flow, at an early stage."
Madsen Gold Corp was up 20 cents at C$2.50 a share on the Toronto exchange Tuesday morning, after seeing a high for the year at C$3.45 on February 26.
((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1641))
